component.name: PyCharm OSS
component.summary: Python IDE for you and your agents

description.p: PyCharm is designed by programmers, for programmers, to provide all the tools you need for productive Python development.
PyCharm provides smart code completion, code inspections, on-the-fly error highlighting and quick-fixes, along with automated code refactorings and rich navigation capabilities.
PyCharm offers great framework-specific support for modern web development frameworks such as Django, Flask, Google App Engine, Pyramid, and web2py.
PyCharm integrates with IPython Notebook, has an interactive Python console, and supports Anaconda as well as multiple scientific packages including matplotlib and NumPy.
In addition to Python, PyCharm supports JavaScript, CoffeeScript, TypeScript, Cython, SQL, HTML/CSS, template languages, AngularJS, Node.js, and more.
A huge collection of tools out of the box: an integrated debugger and test runner; Python profiler; a built-in terminal; and integration with major VCS and built-in Database Tools.

This major release introduces JetBrains Air – a new layer for agentic development that lets you run, track, and verify multi-agent workflows inside your IDE. Alongside Air, version 2026.3 delivers major updates across workspace tooling, Python 3.15 support, and core frameworks:

ul.li: JetBrains Air: Run ACP-compatible agents, track sessions across repositories, and review diffs in context – featuring free agentic coding with Junie Lite.
Workspace support: Dedicated consoles and terminals per subproject running against isolated dependencies, plus quick creation or conversion of workspace members initialized with uv, Hatch, or Poetry.
Python 3.15 lazy imports: Defer module loading to cut startup times in applications with heavy dependencies while retaining full code insight.
FastAPI support (Pro): Visualize endpoint dependencies with interactive graphs that mark yield/return calls and detect circular dependencies.
Redesigned Python interpreter widget: Access and recreate environments organized around the tools that manage them (uv, Poetry, Hatch, and conda).
Deeper Pydantic support: Field constraint checks in the editor, direct navigation from @field_validator, and code completion for model configuration options.

description.p: Read about all the key changes on our what's new page.
Oracle's fixes for CVE-2026-91403 and CVE-2026-114820 were integrated into JBR.
This update fixes several type-checking false positives along with issues in Ruff, Jupyter, Databricks, and interpreter setup:

ul.li: Get correct type inference from Numpy-style docstrings, including favoring type annotations over docstring types and handling tuple[...] with three or more arguments.
Avoid false positive warnings about missing str or repr implementations for IPv4Address/IPv6Address, string literals, and str subtypes.
Avoid a false positive Expected type 'TypedDict | None', got 'dict' instead error when passing a dict where a TypedDict | None is expected.
Get better handling of # type: ignore comments.
Avoid duplicated type checker messages for Pydantic Field.
Avoid a crash loop when using Ruff version 0.16.5 or later.
Generate a new Python environment with uv even when UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT is set.
See Jupyter variables again when using a remote Conda interpreter.
Let the Databricks plugin respect your proxy settings in PyCharm 2026.
Fixed a freeze during dictionary type comparison
PyCharm now shows relevant control flow elements using sticky-lines
Proper type resolutions for __slots__ in enums
Inlay hints for enum auto()
Generic bounds are displayed in parameter info
Unpacking a list no longer produces Any
Completion for TypedDict class parameters like extra_items

description.p: AI agents now work in your Jupyter notebooks and target the right Python environment, marimo notebooks arrive, plus changes to bundled plugins.

ul.li: AI agents like Claude Code and Codex can now create, edit, and run .ipynb notebooks against a live kernel, so data persists across cells.
AI agents now target your project's configured interpreter - uv, Poetry, pip, or conda - so packages land in the right environment instead of a system one.
Open, edit, and run reactive marimo notebooks directly in PyCharm via the new plugin from the marimo team.
We're unbundling and deprecating several low-usage plugins for a leaner, more focused experience.
Explore the redesigned Python Packages window with a collapsible dependency tree and inline Install/Update links.
Find and install packages fast with a new floating search popup that shows the target environment and dependency group.
Read richer type-mismatch errors that break down why the types don't match.
View a type diff for callables and composite types so both sides read the same way.
See fully rendered names and types in inspection tooltips, with clickable links.
PyCharm no longer creates venvs for end-of-life Python 2.7, 3.6, and 3.7. However, you can still use the interpreters created earlier.
Session.get(Entity, id) is now inferred as a model instance rather than the class in SQLAlchemy 2.0.
